tools.title: Arm a trusted targetless Android LLDB server for an explicitly authorized target

inputs.pid: positive integer; AutoCrack controller PID is rejected

guarantees: revalidate package/PID identity and require TracerPid=0 before arming the server
start lldb-server gdbserver on IPv4 loopback without --attach so it reaches LISTEN before target attach
verify helper argv0 and exact targetless gdbserver command line
verify the 127.0.0.1 listener socket inode is owned by the verified helper PID
create the helper PID file under controller ownership before the root helper writes its PID
helper teardown never signals the target PID
detach verification requires TracerPid to return to 0

tools.title: Bounded loopback LLDB client typed attach, observation and execution control
guarantees: construct client endpoint from literal IPv4 loopback bytes rather than localhost resolution
require a verified helper-owned LISTEN socket before CONTROL can connect
after the TCP transport is accepted do not require the single-client LISTEN socket to remain present
post-accept revalidate the same live verified helper, same package/PID and TracerPid=0 immediately before typed vAttach
encode only the already authorized session PID into the fixed typed vAttach packet
after vAttach require TracerPid to equal the verified session helper PID before exposing clientConnected=true
if post-vAttach confirmation fails close the client and safely tear down only the verified helper
no arbitrary raw gdb-remote packet adapter
no register write adapter
no memory write adapter
breakpoints are limited to typed AArch64 hardware execution Z1/z1 packets at positive 4-byte-aligned addresses
software breakpoint Z0/z0 packets are not exposed

automatic stepping anchor prefers the process main TID, reads only its PC, inserts one typed Z1 hardware execution breakpoint at that validated PC, then removes the one-shot anchor after the next continue stop
the thread from each continue stop reply is automatically selected as the next register/step context
after a trusted stop, code context is captured read-only from PC/LR/SP, at most 36 nearby instruction bytes, and /proc/<pid>/maps; no target mutation is used for context

after a trusted stop, bounded call-stack evidence starts at PC and follows at most 16 AArch64 x29 frame records using only bounded memory reads; invalid, cyclic, unmapped, non-monotonic or oversized frame-pointer transitions terminate the unwind as partial evidence
if a usable x29 frame pointer is unavailable, call-stack evidence falls back only to the current PC and mapped LR instead of scanning arbitrary stack memory for guessed return addresses

manual hardware-breakpoint hit counts increment only when a trusted SIGTRAP debugger stop has a matching PC and a breakpoint-compatible reason; step trace and target-signal stops never increment the counter

the automatic one-shot anchor captures its stop context and automatically resumes the target unless the user explicitly requested pause, preventing the target app from remaining frozen after the anchor hit
a bounded 64-entry chronological control timeline preserves attach/continue/anchor/step/recovery/pause transitions with thread and code-location summaries

while live auto-observation is running, a target signal stop is resumed only on the exact thread named by the immediately preceding trusted stop reply using vCont;Cxx:<stopped-thread>;c; the signal is never applied as a process-wide default action
SIGTRAP is auto-passed only when the trusted stop reply explicitly classifies it as reason:signal; hardware-breakpoint and single-step trap stops remain debugger stops
live signal pass-through is decided before qRegisterInfo/maps/code-window capture so runtime-managed signals do not incur repeated heavy observation pauses
memory reads are bounded to 512 bytes in the UI bridge
execution control requires exact CONTROL package/PID authorization
interrupt is a gdb-remote protocol byte, not kill(targetPid)

tools.title: Safely detach an orphaned AutoCrack LLDB helper after controller restart
guarantees: never terminate a tracer from PID alone
revalidate target package identity and current TracerPid immediately before recovery
require tracer argv0 to equal the trusted lldb-server-android binary path
accept only a trusted IPv4 loopback gdbserver command from either legacy --attach or typed client-driven attach sessions
revalidate the exact expected tracer PID immediately before TERM
send TERM only to the verified LLDB helper and never to the target PID
never escalate recovery to SIGKILL
require final target TracerPid=0 for detachVerified=true

tools.title: Start a trusted loopback Frida server bound to one explicitly authorized target

inputs.pid: positive integer; AutoCrack controller PID is rejected

tools.networkScope: literal IPv4 loopback 127.0.0.1 on an AutoCrack-internal managed port only
guarantees: the server is the pinned official Frida 17.17.0 Android arm64 binary from the trusted android-frida toolpack
revalidate package/PID identity and require TracerPid=0 before starting the helper
listen only on literal IPv4 loopback 127.0.0.1; the managed port is selected internally and is never model-controlled
verify helper argv0, exact command line and listener socket ownership before exposing serverReadyForClient=true
the user-authorized package/PID is bound to the session and cannot be changed by the Agent
helper teardown sends TERM only to the reverified Frida helper and never directly signals the target PID

tools.title: Bounded fixed-agent Frida observation for one already-authorized Android process

operations.strategy: fixed network stack and pinning-related class hints only

guarantees: every operation revalidates the bound package/PID immediately before attaching
only the compiled AutoCrack RPC agent bundled in the trusted toolpack may be loaded
no arbitrary JavaScript or Frida REPL is exposed to the Agent
no Memory.write API is exposed
no Interceptor.replace or return-value replacement API is exposed
no arbitrary process spawn or target switching is exposed
native trace accepts only a loaded module basename plus a bounded module-relative hexadecimal offset
native trace rejects targets that do not resolve to an executable memory range
the client unloads the fixed script and detaches after each operation
each operation requires target TracerPid to return to 0 before success is reported
network hints only report bounded loaded-class evidence and never bypass certificate pinning
TLS trace uses fixed Conscrypt read/write observation with bounded duration, event count and plaintext preview bytes
